terms.comment: Any simple or poorly built house: a cottage, hut, cabin or shed (Lewis & Short); also the toy house a child builds (Hor. S. 2.3.247). The thatched casa Rōmulī stood on the Capitol (Vitr. 2.1).

terms.gloss: a shepherd’s or peasant’s hut; a hovel
terms.comment: From tegō, “cover” (Lewis & Short): a roof and little more.

phrases.latin: Potest ex casā vir magnus exīre.
phrases.english: A great man can come out of a hut.

phrases.latin: canis parturiēns cum rogāsset alteram ut fētum in ejus tuguriō dēpōneret, facile impetrāvit
phrases.english: when a dog about to give birth asked another to let her lay her litter in her hut, she easily got her way

sources: Lewis & Short: casa · Lewis & Short: tugurium
